task_instance: Build a production-quality, accessible TaskList feature (React + TypeScript, Vite scaffold) following the skill's component-architecture, state-management, design-token, and WCAG 2.1 AA guidance: colocated files (TaskList.tsx, TaskList.test.tsx, use-task-list.ts, types.ts, TaskList.css), container/presentation split, keyboard-accessible checkbox/delete controls with aria-labels, loading/empty/error/success states, a spacing-scale + semantic-token stylesheet avoiding the 'AI aesthetic' (no purple gradients, minimal rounding, real accent color), and responsive layout. Verified by running the automated test suite (including jest-axe accessibility checks and keyboard-navigation simulation), a TypeScript build, and serving the production build.
evidence: Work dir: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-skill-achievability-compiler/a1321181-416f-5422-8c3b-9ffc8650b51c/scratchpad/exec_ext/addyosmani__agent-skills__frontend-ui-engineering. Scaffolded with `npm create vite@latest . -- --template react-ts`, installed vitest/@testing-library/jest-axe. Implemented src/components/TaskList/{types.ts,use-task-list.ts,TaskList.tsx,TaskListContainer.tsx,TaskList.css,TaskList.test.tsx} plus src/test-setup.ts and vite.config.ts test config, and wired it into src/App.tsx. `npx vitest run` -> 'Test Files 1 passed (1)', 'Tests 10 passed (10)' covering: list role/structure, checked state reflecting task.done, mouse-driven onToggle/onDelete callbacks, full keyboard-only operation (Tab focuses checkbox and delete button, Space toggles, Enter deletes), zero jest-axe violations on TaskList and EmptyState, role=status/role=alert semantics for empty/error states, and aria-busy on the loading skeleton. `npm run build` (tsc -b && vite build) completed with no type errors, producing dist/index.html, dist/assets/index-*.js (222.05 kB), dist/assets/index-*.css (4.30 kB). Started `vite preview` and confirmed via curl that / and the JS bundle both return HTTP 200 and the HTML references the built assets, i.e. the component actually renders and serves as a real production build, not just passing tests in isolation.
